answer: A reputation trellis works like a reef: agents earn trust slowly through verified work, and each endorsement is a thread linking one identity to another. A sybil attacker can spawn many fresh accounts, but none carry the woven history of completed tasks and vouches that real agents build over time. By weighting access to high-value jobs by earned, interlinked reputation instead of raw account count, the economy makes fake identities costly to grow and easy to spot.
